question: Which of the following is the largest phylum of animalia?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Arthropoda__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arthropoda **is the **largest phylum of Animalia**.
 
• An arthropod is an invertebrate animal having an exoskeleton, a segmented body, and paired jointed appendages. 
 
 
• Phylum Arthropoda is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom.
 
• It was first created by Von Seibold in 1845.
 
• Around two-thirds of all named species on earth come under phylum arthropods.
 
• The body of arthropods is covered by a chitinous exoskeleton.
 
• Phylum Arthropoda has jointed appendages.
 
• The respiratory organs of arthropods are gills, book gills, book lungs, or tracheal system.
 
• The circulatory system in Arthropoda is of open type.
 
• Excretion in Arthropoda takes place through malpighian tubules.
 
• Examples of Phylum Arthropoda are Cockroach, Prawn, Crab, Scorpion, Centipede, Housefly, Ticks, and Mites.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mollusca:

 
 
• Mollusca is the second-largest phylum of invertebrate animals after the Arthropoda.
 
• The members are known as molluscs or mollusks.
 
• Around 85,000 extant species of molluscs are recognized.
 
• The number of fossil species is estimated between 60,000 and 100,000 additional species.
 
 
 
• Ctenophora:
 
 
• Ctenophora comprise a phylum of invertebrate animals that live in marine waters worldwide.
 
• They are notable for the groups of cilia they use for swimming, and they are the largest animals to swim with the help of cilia.
 
• Depending on the species, adult ctenophores range from a few millimeters to 1.5 m in size.
 
 
 
• Platyhelminthes:
 
 
• They have a dorsoventrally flattened body, hence are called flatworms.
 
• These are mostly endoparasites found in animals including human beings.
 
• Flatworms are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, and acoelomate animals with organ level of organization.
 
• Examples: Taenia (Tapeworm) and fasciola (Liver fluke).
 
 
 
• **Annelida :**
 
 
• The body is long, thin, soft, and metamerically segmented.
 
• Locomotion takes place through Setae made up of Chitin.
 
• The alimentary canal is well developed.
 
• The nervous system is normal and blood is red.
 
• Excretion by nephridia.
 
• Both unisexual and bisexual.
 
• Example: Earthworm.
 
 
 
• Chordata**:**
 
 
• Chordates include vertebrates and invertebrates that have a notochord.
 
• During some period of their life cycle, chordates possess a notochord.
 
• Animals in the phylum Chordata must have:
 
 
• A notochord
 
• A dorsal hollow nerve cord
 
• Pharyngeal slits
 
• Post-anal tail.
 
 
 
• Chordates are also bilaterally symmetric and have a circulatory system.
 
• Chordates also have a closed circulatory system.
 
• Chordates are capable of locomotion by means of muscular movements at some stage in life.
